attributes.body_ja:
「に至（いた）っては」は、ある特定（とくてい）のカテゴリーの中（なか）で、最（もっと）も極端（きょくたん）な例（れい）を示（しめ）すときの表現（ひょうげん）です。「(A) については (B) だ」「特（とく）に (A) は (B) だ」「(A) を最（もっと）も極端（きょくたん）な例（れい）として、(B) だ」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「に至（いた）っては」を構成（こうせい）するのは、格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」と、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「至（いた）る」（意味（いみ）：頂点（ちょうてん）に行（い）き着（つ）く）のテ形（けい）、主題（しゅだい）を示（しめ）す副助詞（ふくじょし）の「は」です。そのため、文字通（もじどお）りの意味（いみ）は「(A) を頂点（ちょうてん）として (B)」になるでしょう。

「に至（いた）っては」は、名詞（めいし）、または名詞化（めいしか）した句（く）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「至（いた）る」という動詞（どうし）そのものが極端（きょくたん）な状態（じょうたい）や限界（げんかい）に達（たっ）することを表（あらわ）すため、「に至（いた）っては」は予想外（よそうがい）なことや衝撃的（しょうげきてき）なことを表（あらわ）すために使（つか）われやすいです。また、この表現（ひょうげん）は、基本的（きほんてき）に話（はな）し手（て）にとって望（のぞ）ましくない事柄（ことがら）に使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
に至（いた）っては is an expression which presents the most extreme example for something from within a specific category. Due to this, it will usually be translated as 'when it comes to (A), (B)', 'in particular to (A) is (B)', or 'with (A) as the most extreme example, (B)'.

This is a combination of the case-marking particle に, the て-form of the る-Verb 至（いた）る 'to climax', or 'to culminate in', and the adverbial particle は in its standard role of presenting a topic. In this way, the literal meaning of 'culminating within (A) is (B)' is quite close to the nuance of the English translations.

に至（いた）っては will appear following nouns, or nominalized phrases.

Caution

As the verb 至（いた）る itself is used to present extreme examples or locations that are considered to be right 'on the precipice' of something, に至（いた）っては will primarily present things that are surprising or astonishing in some way. This is primarily only used when the example itself is quite negative or unfavorable.

Both relate to reaching a point, but the function is different. に至って・に至り marks the point at which a result, realization, or change finally occurs after preceding circumstances, often corresponding to ‘not until’ or ‘only when,’ as in 先輩に注意されるに至って、自分の間違いに気づいた (‘I didn’t realize my mistake until I was warned by a senior.’). に至っては is used to single out an extreme or noteworthy example within a broader situation, adding emphasis similar to ‘what’s more’ or ‘even,’ as in 母に至ってはインターネットさえ使えない (‘What’s more, my mother can’t even use the internet.’).

first_relatable.title: に至って・に至り
first_relatable.meaning: When it came to, Only when, Only after, Go as far as

second_relatable.title: に至っては
second_relatable.meaning: When it comes to, As for, In particular, What is worse or more

attributes.body: Both refer to an extreme point or example, but with opposite nuance. に至っても means ‘even after reaching (that point),’ emphasizing that a situation or attitude does not change despite time, experience, or progress, as in 注意されるに至っても態度は変わらなかった ('Even after being warned, his attitude did not change.'). に至っては singles out a specific case or stage as especially noteworthy or extreme within a broader situation, often with emphasis like ‘when it comes to’ or ‘even,’ as in 母に至ってはインターネットさえ使えない ('When it comes to my mother, she can’t even use the internet.').

second_relatable.title: に至っては
second_relatable.meaning: When it comes to, As for, In particular, What is worse or more

attributes.body: Both expressions can convey the idea of 'particularly', but in different ways. に至っては presents an extreme example of something previously introduced. For example, when talking about a region with a lot of snowfall, A市に至っては60センチも積もることがある ('In particular, city A sometimes has accumulation of 60 cm.'). In contrast, に限って is often used when some unexpected/undesired action happens 'particularly' or 'only' at certain times, e.g. 忙しい時に限って誘ってくる ('He invites me particularly/only when I'm busy.').
